stem: Under the accrual basis of accounting, why are adjustments made while preparing the final accounts?
options: To record all cash received and paid during the year in the final accounts
To take revenues on an earned basis and expenses on an incurred basis
To show every asset of the business at its current market value
To make the totals of the trial balance agree before the year closes
explanation: Correct option: (B). The accrual concept requires revenues to be taken when earned and expenses when incurred, not when cash is received or paid, so items relating to other periods or still unrecorded must be adjusted. (A) describes the cash basis. (C) is wrong because assets are not revalued to market value through these adjustments. (D) is wrong because adjustments are made after the trial balance is prepared and are not meant to correct its agreement.

Capital = 3,00,000 + interest 15,000 + net profit 1,35,000 = Rs. 4,50,000; the interest reduces profit but is added back to capital, so the effect is neutralised. (A) forgets to add the interest to capital. (B) adds the interest to the profit before interest, counting it twice. (C) computes commission on profit before charging it (16,500).
